text:
jordan_support: Hey team, customer on Private deployment (acme-med) reporting intermittent connection resets to the inference endpoint. They see 502 / TLS handshake failures and occasional DNS timeouts. Started ~2 hours ago.
sara_infra: Can you paste the client error sample and whether this is only from one AZ or multiple? Also did they report any packet captures yet?
jordan_support: client log: `rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection reset by peer` and browser shows `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` on streaming requests. Only from instances in us-east-1a (per their infra team). They ran curl and sometimes it times out: `curl: (28) Operation timed out after 30001 ms`.
ops_oncall: Quick checklist — NAT/gateway asymmetry, stateful SG vs stateless NACL, ephemeral port range, DNS cache. Have them run tcpdump on the inference host while reproducing.
sara_infra: Agreed. Stateless NACLs will drop return packets if ephemeral ports are not allowed back. Ask them to capture on the instance facing the internet egress path. Example tcpdump filter:
```bash
sudo tcpdump -n -i any host <customer-client-ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/trace.pcap
```
Also capture the client side if possible: `tcpdump -nn -i eth0 src <client-ip> and dst host <inference-ip>`.
jordan_support: I asked and they uploaded a pcap. Quick glance shows lots of SYN retransmits and then a few SYN,ACKs with no ACK from client. Also see `RST` from the inference host sometimes.
ops_oncall: That pattern often means return path is being blocked or NAT device is rewriting source in a way the client drops. Check VPC flow logs for REJECTs and the NACL rule numbers. Example AWS commands they can run:
```bash
aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-xxxxx
aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-xxxxx
```
Look for explicit DENY in NACLs for ephemeral ranges (1024-65535) or very narrow ephemeral port windows.
sara_infra: Also verify the customer's egress allowlist (on their corporate FW) isn't dropping high source ports. Some corporate middleboxes do deep packet inspection and drop flows that look unexpected.
jordan_support: They ran `sudo conntrack -L | grep <client-ip>` and saw lots of CLOSE_WAIT / TIME_WAIT entries but also entries disappearing quickly.
ops_oncall: Another useful check: capture the three-way handshake with `sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -w /tmp/syn.pcap 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-ack) != 0'` to see who is sending/acknowledging. If you see SYN from client, SYN,ACK from server, and then no ACK, the ACK was likely blocked on return. If ACK present but RST soon after, server may be rejecting based on TLS or application.
sara_infra: Ask them to temporarily open a broad ephemeral allow rule on the NACL for test (both directions) and see if errors stop. Example NACL entries (temporary, highest priority):
```text
Ingress: rule 100 allow tcp 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0
Egress:  rule 100 allow tcp 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0
```
Remind them NACL is stateless so both sides must be allowed.
jordan_support: I pushed those instructions. They just replied: after opening ephemeral range inbound they see steady connections, errors dropped to zero in tests for ~10 minutes. When they revert the rule, errors come back.
ops_oncall: That's a smoking gun for NACL blocking return path. Recommend they narrow the rule to the specific client CIDR and keep it temporary, then track down why the original NACL was so restrictive (automation, terraform drift). Also check for any intermediate NAT/inspection box that might rewrite ports.
sara_infra: One more thing — DNS timeouts could be a symptom: if the client uses external resolvers and egress to UDP/53 is blocked on ephemeral return, look for `unreachable` in VPC flow logs for the resolver IPs.
jordan_support: I'll write up a short RCA for the customer: cause = stateless NACL blocking ephemeral return ports -> symptom = TLS handshake resets / connection resets / curl timeouts -> mitigation = allow ephemeral range or restrict to client CIDR temporarily; long term = fix IaC to open expected ranges or route via NAT with proper mapping. Will include tcpdump snippets and the pcap for their team.
infra-bot: ticket #CUST-18291 updated: assigned to sara_infra. :white_check_mark:
ops_oncall: If they want, we can offer to run a config review (quick consult) to harden rules without broadening to 1024-65535 globally.
jordan_support: Thanks all — letting customer know next steps and closing loop once they confirm permanent fix. :thumbsup:
